about_feature_fast_dev_desc: Vite keeps iteration tight, making changes to routes, styles, and server code quick to validate.
about_feature_responsive_desc: Layouts hold together on narrow screens without becoming too dense.
about_feature_type_safety_desc: Type boundaries across routes, loaders, actions, and RPC keep the demo reliable.
about_features_intro: The goal is not visual noise or framework spectacle, but a readable demo surface that iterates quickly and behaves predictably.
about_hero_body: This demo keeps the stack deliberately lean so that React Router, Hono, Vanilla Extract, and typed request flows are easy to inspect rather than hidden behind abstractions.
about_hero_lead: Architecture, stack, and design decisions in one place.
about_next_errors_desc: See boundaries, status codes, and recovery behavior under failure conditions.
about_next_hono_rpc_desc: Follow a typed client-to-server exchange through Hono RPC.
about_next_intro: After the overview, use the remaining routes to inspect rendering, data flow, and failure handling separately.
about_next_ssr_desc: View request-time rendering, timing data, and server-held state on a server-owned page.
about_stack_frontend_desc: The presentation layer keeps routes, components, styles, and icons easy to inspect.
about_stack_intro: Rather than burying the application behind a thick framework facade, each layer is exposed so you can read how the demo is assembled.
about_stack_runtime_desc: The server side is deliberately lean so rendering and request flow are visible rather than concealed.
about_stack_title: The stack stays lean so the concepts stay legible.
error_code_default_detail: This route formats both thrown responses and runtime exceptions into a consistent SSR error view.
error_code_default_scenario_note: This code path is not part of the curated examples.
error_code_default_summary: The loader intentionally failed so the route boundary can take over.
error_code_footer_note: Thrown responses preserve their HTTP semantics; thrown runtime errors are still caught here, but the boundary surfaces them as an application failure.
error_code_pending_message: This route is designed to throw before the normal component renders
error_code_row_1_body: The boundary normalizes the thrown value into a readable status surface.
error_code_row_2_body: The error starts in the route loader and ends at the route boundary.
error_code_row_3_body: Compare different routes to see boundary behavior across status families.
error_code_section_intro: This route throws in the loader, then the route-level boundary renders the final page you are viewing.
error_code_value_rendered_by: ErrorBoundary in the same route file
error_scenario_401_detail: Simulates a protected route that requires credentials before the request proceeds.
error_scenario_401_summary: The request is understood, but the user is not authenticated.
error_scenario_403_detail: Demonstrates the difference between being unauthenticated and being blocked after authentication.
error_scenario_403_summary: The request is known, but the current actor is not permitted to proceed.
error_scenario_404_detail: Throws a 404 response so the route boundary can render the missing-resource state.
error_scenario_404_summary: Use when a path or resource should report that it does not exist.
error_scenario_500_detail: Models an internal server failure where the route cannot produce a normal response.
error_scenario_500_summary: A general server-side failure that becomes an HTTP error response.
error_scenario_502_detail: Represents an upstream dependency that responded incorrectly or with unusable data.
error_scenario_502_summary: The application responded, but an upstream dependency failed first.
error_scenario_503_detail: Useful for downtime and maintenance states, where the route should announce temporary unavailability.
error_scenario_503_summary: The service is up enough to respond, but not ready to fulfill the request.
error_scenario_runtime_detail: Throws a normal JavaScript Error rather than a Response, letting you compare two failure modes. Server-side logs retain the current app.session_id for matching with browser issues.
error_scenario_runtime_summary: A runtime exception escaped the route logic and was caught by the route boundary.
errors_hero_body: Use this page to jump into thrown response errors, runtime exceptions, and the route boundaries that surface them. The hub itself is pre-rendered; each case below is a live server-rendered incident surface.
errors_hero_lead: A static index of failure paths the app can intentionally trigger.
errors_notice_1_body: /errors does not throw, so it is safe to pre-render.
errors_notice_1_detail: It acts as a navigation map into the error cases, not an error screen itself.
errors_notice_2_body: /errors/:code throws from the loader to simulate real failures.
errors_notice_2_detail: This makes the page useful for seeing SSR, status code, and response header behavior when a route does not resolve normally.
errors_notice_3_body: A route boundary catches the failure and transforms it into the final visual surface.
errors_notice_3_detail: Meaning the 404, 500, or runtime page you see is intentionally designed by the route, not a browser fallback.
errors_section_intro_choose: Each route below shows a different way the application can fail, and how a route-level boundary reshapes that failure into something inspectable.
errors_section_intro_notice: The interesting split is between the static entry page, the dynamic route loader, and the boundary that formats both response errors and thrown exceptions.
errors_spacer_intro: Start with /errors/404 or /errors/runtime to compare a thrown response and a thrown JavaScript error.
hero_body: Five routes make SSR, RPC, layout, boundaries, and architecture readable rather than turning the homepage into an information panel.
hero_lead: Rendering, routing, and recovery in a lean full-stack demo.
holy_grail_article_desc: The root route holds the document shell. This route owns the visible structure, so the holy grail stays inside the page, not leaking into the app shell.
holy_grail_article_title: Header on top, main in the middle, footer at the bottom.
holy_grail_footer_note: Static route • Pre-rendered at build • No loader
holy_grail_layout_main_desc: The center track scales and stays readable across widths.
holy_grail_layout_note_2: Page shell is a grid with header, main, and footer rows.
holy_grail_layout_note_3: Center track uses grid columns so sidebars never steal focus.
holy_grail_layout_right_desc: Status, notes, and related links that should not dominate the flow.
holy_grail_left_desc: This rail keeps supplementary information close to the main without requiring the primary content to carry everything.
holy_grail_left_note_1: Fixed navigation does not fight the primary reading flow.
holy_grail_left_note_2: Useful metadata belongs in a sidebar, not in the homepage copy.
holy_grail_left_note_3: When the sidebar collapses on mobile, the layout still works.
holy_grail_nested_desc: Nested shells let the center track adapt to article width rather than the viewport.
holy_grail_nested_title: Header, main, footer inside an article.
holy_grail_right_desc: A sidebar is where reference materials, status, or auxiliary content live without forcing the central article to double as everything.
holy_grail_right_note_1: Fixed sidebars form the classic holy grail silhouette.
holy_grail_right_note_2: Center column is the only region that should stretch significantly.
holy_grail_right_note_3: Headers and footers frame the content without trapping it.
hono_rpc_error_retry: Try reloading the Hono RPC page
hono_rpc_hero_body: The initial response comes through a route loader, then the same endpoint can be revalidated client-side via the Hono RPC client.
hono_rpc_hero_lead: A typed request surface that refreshes without leaving the route.
hono_rpc_label_initial_source_value: Route loader / Shared API response factory
hono_rpc_row_1_body: Return value of GET /api/rpc/hello, first rendered by the loader, then refreshable on demand.
hono_rpc_row_2_body: Route and API are linked through a generated Hono client rather than hand-writing fetch strings.
hono_rpc_row_3_body: This page demonstrates where SSG, hydration, revalidation, and typed API calls intersect.
hono_rpc_section_intro: The same typed endpoint drives both the initial route load and the in-page refresh action.
hono_rpc_section_title: The response is live and refetchable.
hono_rpc_value_client_refresh: The button fetches fresh RPC data without reloading the page.
hono_rpc_value_hydrated_data: The initial server-rendered response stays visible while the client fetches fresh data on demand.
hono_rpc_value_prerendered_shell: Routes can produce static structure at build time.
hono_rpc_value_typed_boundary: The hc() client keeps route code aligned with the API contract.
meta_about_desc: Architecture, stack, and design decisions for a React Router + Hono demo.
meta_error_code_desc: A dynamic error route demonstrating thrown responses and runtime failures.
meta_error_code_title: Error case demo · React Router + Hono demo
meta_errors_desc: Explore thrown response errors and runtime failures in the React Router + Hono demo.
meta_errors_title: Error handling demo · React Router + Hono demo
meta_holy_grail_desc: A pre-rendered holy grail layout demo with header, main, footer, and responsive side rails.
meta_holy_grail_title: Holy grail layout · React Router + Hono demo
meta_hono_rpc_desc: A typed Hono RPC demo with client refresh capability
meta_hono_rpc_title: Hono RPC demo · React Router + Hono demo

route_about_description: Project overview, stack notes, and migration decisions for the application.
route_errors_description: Error routes and boundary behavior for failure states, status codes, and recovery.
route_holy_grail_description: Header, main, and footer arranged in a classic holy grail app shell.
route_hono_rpc_description: Typed client and server calls through Hono without ceremony.
route_ssr_description: Request-time rendering, timing data, and server-held state displayed on the page.
routes_section_intro: Each entry isolates one concern so you can inspect the stack piece by piece rather than decoding everything at once.
routes_section_title: Start with one route. The rest is in view.
ssr_hero_body: Loaders execute on every request, forward timing metadata, and can read the Hono context before the page reaches the browser.
ssr_hero_lead: This route renders on the server every time.
ssr_hono_context_desc: Data forwarded from the Hono request context into a React Router loader via RouterContextProvider.
ssr_live_response_desc: Request-specific data the SSR loader produces before the page is delivered.
ssr_loader_message: This page is rendered on the server on every request!
ssr_section_response_intro: These values are produced during the request, then serialized into the rendered HTML and response headers.
ssr_section_response_title: The current response came from the server.
ssr_section_verify_intro: This route is for verifying, not just viewing. These checks make the rendering mode obvious.
ssr_section_verify_title: How to verify the page is really SSR.
ssr_verify_compare_value: Unlike / or /about, this route is not SSG. Unlike a pure CSR interface, its first HTML already contains the server response.
ssr_verify_desc: Use the browser and network tools to confirm the response is produced at request time.
ssr_verify_headers_value: Open the network tab and check Server-Timing to verify loader execution time.
ssr_verify_refresh_value: The timestamp changes on every request because the loader runs server-side each time.
